title: Day 786: Two US Citizens Disappear in Culiacán Within 48 Hours
detail: Two US citizens vanished in separate incidents in Culiacán within a two-day span, days after a third American was shot dead in Mazatlán on September 14. José Antonio Castro Meza, 29, was last seen around 10:45 PM on Tuesday, September 15, driving a gray Geely EX2 through the La Campiña neighborhood; his vehicle was found abandoned on Thursday morning, September 17, on Liberalismo street in the Lázaro Cárdenas neighborhood near Parque 87, but he was not located. Separately, on the morning of September 17, armed men intercepted Luis Mario Zúñiga Ramos, 49 — owner of a long-established Culiacán jewelry business — as he arrived at his shop in the Plaza Real, Tres Ríos sector, forcing him out of his armored Audi and into another vehicle. State, municipal and Army search operations were underway for both men as of the report, with no arrests or public leads announced.

title: Day 786: Woman Shot Dead in Hammock at Her Home in Mazatlán's Francisco I. Madero Neighborhood
detail: During the afternoon of Thursday, September 17, 2026, a 42-year-old woman identified as Sofía was shot and killed while resting in a hammock inside her home in the Francisco I. Madero neighborhood of Mazatlán. Armed men arriving in a gray vehicle entered the residence and opened fire, hitting her at least twice — in the neck and torso. Navy personnel were first responders, followed by firefighter-paramedics who could not revive her. The case marked the eighth femicide recorded in Mazatlán that month and pushed Sinaloa's September 2026 tally of women killed to 19, already surpassing the 73 total femicides recorded across all of 2025.

title: Day 786: Armed Pursuit in Mazatlán's El Toreo Neighborhood Leaves Motorcyclist and Driver Dead
detail: Around 7:00 PM on Thursday, September 17, 2026, gunmen on a motorcycle pursued a white Toyota Yaris along Calle Jesús Solórzano near Avenida La Marina in the El Toreo neighborhood of Mazatlán, firing roughly 11 shots at the driver, identified as Abraham 'N'. During the attack, a hotel cook named Edwin 'N', who was riding his own motorcycle on the same street, was struck and killed by a stray bullet. Abraham was taken to the General Hospital, where he died of his wounds hours later. The Fiscalía General del Estado had not confirmed whether the two killings were connected to a targeted pursuit.

media.caption: Scene of the pursuit-shooting that killed a motorcyclist and a driver in Mazatlán's El Toreo neighborhood, September 17, 2026

title: Day 786: 19-Year-Old Motorcyclist Shot Dead in Culiacán's Díaz Ordaz Neighborhood
detail: At approximately 4:00 PM on Thursday, September 17, 2026, a 19-year-old identified as Ovier de Jesús was intercepted while riding his motorcycle on Calle Sebastián Allende, between Ciro Ceballos and Joaquín Berlanga, in the Gustavo Díaz Ordaz neighborhood of Culiacán. An armed assailant shot him multiple times, killing him at the scene; several spent cartridges were recovered. Municipal police, Mexican Army and SSPC personnel responded, and family members from his home in the Progreso neighborhood later identified the body.

media.caption: Authorities at the scene of the fatal shooting of 19-year-old motorcyclist Ovier de Jesús in Culiacán's Díaz Ordaz neighborhood, September 17, 2026

title: Day 786: Windshield Washer Shot Dead at Villa Unión Gas Station — Second Killing at Same Site in 9 Days
detail: At around 7:45 PM on Thursday, September 17, 2026, armed men in a black vehicle shot and killed a windshield washer working at a gas station at the intersection of Boulevard Niños Héroes and the free Mazatlán–Durango highway, at the southern exit of Villa Unión, Mazatlán. The victim, wearing a plaid long-sleeved shirt, died at the scene before emergency responders arrived. It was the second fatal shooting at the same gas station in nine days, following the September 8 killing of 59-year-old motorcyclist Guillermo Artemio at the same location.
